issues.description: mathimpl.py uses sys.version_info without importing sys
issues.detail: The patch adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` guards in both numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py, but the diff shows no `import sys` added to either file. The precondition of the guarded statement is that `sys` is a bound name; the author has not established it. On a Python 3.11+ install this file will fail at import time with NameError, which is a defect any test execution would expose immediately. This is the textbook case of code that has been written without reasoning about what must be true on entry.

issues.description: Math_unary registration block is structurally broken by misplaced blank line / dedent
issues.detail: In numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py the previously trailing blank line inside the class body was removed and replaced by `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` at module scope, immediately adjacent to the class. The post-condition the author presumably intends is: Math_unary is registered as the type signature for math.exp2 in addition to all existing unary math functions. But Math_unary is the same shared ConcreteTemplate used to register sin, cos, tan, exp, log, etc., and rebinding the name via `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` works only because infer_global mutates the registry as a side effect; the reassignment is misleading and the structural placement (no blank line separating from the class, then a hard transition to module-level if) makes the control flow harder to read than necessary. Worse, it is `sys`-dependent without an `import sys` shown for this file either (the diff adds `import sys`, good — this one is fine), so confirm only this part. The real P0 here is that there is no blank line between the class body and the conditional, which on some formatters / lint configurations is a syntactic smell and on a future edit invites accidentally pulling the if into the class body.

issues.description: TESTED-NOT-PROVED: no correctness reasoning about LLVM llvm.exp2 semantics vs CPython math.exp2
issues.detail: The author claims math.exp2 support by binding it to the LLVM intrinsic `llvm.exp2`. The precondition required is: for every input value math.exp2 accepts (including the integer types listed in the test — int16..uint64), llvm.exp2 produces a result bit-identical (or at minimum, equally well-defined under IEEE-754) to CPython's math.exp2. No such argument is offered. The test uses values {-2,-1,-2,2,1,2,.1,.2}; this is a presence-of-bugs test, not an absence-of-bugs proof. Edge cases not exercised: +/-inf, NaN, subnormals, very large positive (overflow to inf), very large negative (underflow to 0), and the integer-to-float conversion path for uint64 near 2^63. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence.

issues.description: SMUGGLED-GOTO: version-gating via scattered top-level `if` instead of a single guarded registration site
issues.detail: The same `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` predicate is repeated in three separate modules (mathdecl.py, cpython/mathimpl.py, np/math/mathimpl.py) with no single source of truth. This is a goto disguised as a conditional: control jumps over a registration in each module independently, and a future maintainer changing the minimum Python version must find and update three call sites without a compiler to remind them. A structured approach declares the supported intrinsics once (e.g., a tuple gated on PYVERSION imported from numba.core.utils, as the test file already does) and iterates. The test file imports PYVERSION from numba.core.utils; the implementation files should do the same instead of reaching for `sys.version_info` directly, which is also inconsistent with project convention.

issues.description: Newsfile missing trailing newline; minor but documents a lack of care
issues.detail: docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files end with a newline; rst toolchains and git diff machinery both behave better when this invariant holds. A reviewer who is willing to ship a file without a terminating newline is a reviewer who has not yet developed the habit of asking what invariants every artifact in the tree must satisfy.

issues.description: Test value list duplicates -2 and 2, reducing coverage
issues.detail: `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` repeats -2 and 2. This is copied from the math.exp test above, which already had the same defect. The set of distinct inputs is therefore smaller than the list length suggests. Not load-bearing for correctness — see the TESTED-NOT-PROVED note — but if one is going to test rather than prove, one should at least test distinct points.

issues.description: Newsfile prose is redundant and uninformative
issues.detail: The body of 10276.new_feature.rst reads, in its entirety: title `Add support for math.exp2.` followed by the body `Support for math.exp2 is added.` The body restates the title with no additional information — no mention of the Python version requirement, no mention that the implementation routes to llvm.exp2, no mention of supported types. A reader of the changelog learns nothing from the second sentence that the first did not already tell them.

review.summary: UNREASONED and at least one outright defect. The patch adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` guards in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py without adding `import sys` to those files — a NameError waiting at import time on the very Python versions the guard is meant to enable. The author has demonstrated no reasoning about why llvm.exp2 is semantically equivalent to CPython's math.exp2 across all input types and edge cases; the eight-element test vector with duplicates is a presence-of-bugs probe, not an absence-of-bugs proof, and it omits inf, NaN, overflow, underflow, and the large-integer conversion path. The version predicate is smuggled across three files instead of expressed once; the test file already imports PYVERSION from numba.core.utils and the implementation should do the same. REFUSED in its current form; the import bug is non-negotiable, and the correctness argument and structural placement should be tightened before this is merged.
